case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 03.07.2018 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No6326 of 2018 AND judgment and order dated 11.0.3.2021 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka)
full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J.: This Civil Appeal and the Leave Petition are disposed of by this common judgment as the said appeal and the leave petition both involve common questions of law and facts and the parties are also same.
2. The Civil Appeal No.28 of 2020 has been directed against the judgment and order dated 03.07.2018 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.6326 of 2008 making the Rule absolute and thereby directing the writ-respondents to consider the writ-petitioner's case to be promoted to the post of Deputy Inspector General (DIG) in accordance with Law with immediate effect declaring the impugned notification No.44.00.0000.094.04.073.13 (Part-621) dated 09.05.2018 issued under the signature of the Writ-respondent No.5 attaching the writ-petitioner to the non-existing post from the present Post of Commandant (Police Super), Range Reserve Force, Dhaka to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
3. The Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.145b of 2021 is directed against the judgment and order dated 11.03.2021 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka in Appeal No.92 of 2018 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and order dated 24.01.2018 passed by the Administrative Tribunal No.3, Dhaka in A.T. Case No.170 of 2017(new), 243 of 2017 (old) allowing the case with some modification.
4. The facts leading to filing both the cases as narrated by the writ-petitioner in short are that the present respondent as writ-petitioner filed Writ Petition No.6326 of 2018 before the High Court Division challenging the impugned order bearing No.44.00.0000.094.04.073.13 (Part-621) dated 09.05.2018 issued under the signature of the writ-respondent No.5 transfer-ring and attaching the present respondent-writ petitioner from his present post Commandant (Police Super), Range Reserve Force, Dhaka to Police Super, Police Directorate, Dhaka which amounting to reduction in rank and depriving the right to exercise his official power with malafide intention to harass and embarrass him. The writ-petitioner being a valiant and dedicated police officer of Bangladesh Police, he had been serving in the Department of Police with his utmost sincerity and dignity. The writ-petitioner appeared in the 17th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) Examination and success-fully qualified in all the examinations of the 17th BCS in which the writ-petitioner stood 4th in the combined merit list and 1st in the Police Cadre and thus he had selected for joining in the Department of Police, Bangladesh. The writ-petitioner had been finally selected as an apprentice Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP), and in pursuance of the said order, the writ-petitioner joined the Department of Police as an apprentice ASP, Bangladesh Police on 22.02.1998. During his service the writ-petitioner appeared in the depart-mental examination for the first time in the year 1998 and stood first in the said examination even before completion of his basic training at Bangladesh Police Academy, Sarda, Rajshahi, which was subsequently published in the official Gazette on 1510.1998 and sent to the writ-petitioner for his record by a letter dated 25.11.1998. In September, 1999 upon successful completion of the basic training at Bangladesh Police Academy, Sarda, the writ-petitioner was awarded the Best Rider Prize and received a Meddle from the then Hon'ble Prime Minister as a recognition to his extraordinary performance. Thereafter, Bangladesh Public Service Commission by its gazette notification dated 10.12.2002 published a list of the names of the Officers, who passed the examination for the promotion to the Senior Scale Officer, where the name of the writ-petitioner was also included under serial No.52 since he had success-fully passed the examination. The writ-petitioner joined the Department of Police in the year 1998 and passed all the professional examinations with outstanding results and also successfully completed a number of courses. The average Annual Confidential Report (ACR) of the writ-petitioner was more than 95% from the year 2010 to 2014, which is an extra ordinary achievement for ACR evaluation. The writ-respondent No.3issued notification bearing memo No.44.00.0000.094.06. 04116-230 dated 23.02.2016 intimating the Officers of BCS Police Cadre from serial Nos.1 to 27 that they were being promoted to the post of Additional Deputy Inspector General of Police (Additional DIG) of Grade-4. However, to the utter dismay of the writ-petitioner, his name was not included in the list despite the fact that he possessed all the qualifications. The writ-petitioner, thereafter, under compulsion had to file Writ Petition No.5488 of 2016 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. Subsequently, the High Court Division after hearing the parties and considering all the relevant facts disposed of the Rule with sonic observations, directing the writ-respondents to include the writ-petitioner in the list of promotion to Inc post of Additional DIG, Police in Grade-A and place him in serial No.7 within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order.
5. Thereafter, the writ-respondents preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2235 of 2016 before this Division. Upon hearing the parties, this Division observed that "there was no dispute that the writ-petitioner was a brilliant officer and he stood first in his BCS Examination and there was no stigma in his service record throughout his career. Mr. Mahbubey Alain had refrained from making any comment regarding the efficiency and capability of the writ-petitioner to be considered for promotion to the next high-er post..." However this Division disposed of the said Civil Petition by observing that if the writ-petitioner redresses of his grievances before the Administrative Tribunal that the Administrative Tribunal shall hear and dispose of the petitioner within 6(six) months from the date of filing of the case.
6. Thereafter, the writ-petitioner filed a case before the Administrative Tribunal being A.T. Case No.243 of 2017 which was renumbered as A.T. Case No.170 of 2017. Upon hearing the parties at length the Administrative Tribunal No.2, Dhaka by its judgment and order dated 24.01.2018 allowed the said case with observations that “গত ২৭/১২/২০১৫ ইং তারিখের বিভাগীয় পদোন্নতি কমিটির সভায় প্রার্থীর সিদ্ধান্ত পত্রে কোনরুপ সুপারিশ ব্যতিরেকে নিষ্ক্রীয় ভূমিকা পালন করা সঠিক হয় নাই। যাহা নি:সন্দেহে প্রার্থীকে অন্যায়ভাবে ন্যায্য পদোন্নতি থেকে বঞ্চিত করার বলে অত্র ট্রাইব্যুনাল মনে করে। যাহা বাংলাদেশ সংবিধানের ১৯,২৭ ও ২৯ অনুচ্ছেদ লংঘন হইয়াছে বলে প্রতীয়মান হয়।” The operative portion of the judgment of the Administrative Tribunal was that “আদেশ হয় যে, অত্র প্রশাসনিক ট্রাইব্যুনালে দায়েরকৃত প্রার্থীর মামলাটি প্রতিপক্ষের বিরুদ্ধে দোতরফা সূত্রে শুনানী অন্তে বিনা খরচায় মঞ্জুর করা হইল। একই সাথে বিগত ২৩/০২/২০১৬ ইং তারিখে জারিকৃত প্রজ্ঞাপনের ৭নং ক্রমিকে প্রাথথীর নাম প্রতিস্থাপন করিয়া উক্ত তারিখ হইতে অতি:ডিআইজি, গ্রেড-৪, জাতীয় বেতন ক্কেল/২০১৫ টাকা ৫০,০০০/- হইতে ৭১,২০০/- পদে ভূতাপেক্ষভাবে পদোন্নতি প্রদান করতঃ আগামী ০৭ দিনের মধ্যে সমস্ত বেতন, ভাতাদি, জেষ্ঠ্যতা ও চাকুরীর অন্যান্য সুবিধাদি প্রদানের বিষয়াদি বিবেচনার জন্য প্রতিপক্ষকে নির্দেশ দেওয়া গেল।” Subsequently, the writ-petitioner submitted an application on 25.01.2018 along with certified copy of the judgment and order of the Administrative Tribunal dated 24.01.2018 to the writ-respondent No.1 through the writ-respondent No.4 to execute and com-ply with the order of the Tribunal. The said prayer of the writ-petitioner was duly forwarded to the writ-respondent No.1., Secretary, Public Security Division, Ministry of Home Affairs through writ-respondent No.4, Inspector General of Police vide its office memo dated 28.01.2018. The writ-respondents by its letter dated 13.02.2018 requested the Solicitor Wing, Law and Justice Division, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs to prefer an appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against the aforesaid judgment and order of the Administrative Tribunal.
7. In response to the above request of the Police Head Quarter, the Solicitor in its letter. dated 28.02.2018 provided its opinion informing the writ-respondents that there was no merit to prefer any appeal against the said judgment and order of the Administrative Tribunal and if any such appeal is filed that would be wastage of money of the public exchequer and thus provided clear opinion not to file any appeal against the aforesaid judgment of the Administrative Tribunal. Thereafter, writ-respondents proposed the downgraded promotee officers whose names appeared in the list under serial Nos.7,8,9,10,11 and 13 to be promoted again as Deputy Inspector General (DIG) current charge. 'Me writ-petitioner having possessed the same criteria and better quality deserved to be promoted to the post of DIG in the light of judgment and order dated 09.06.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.5388 of 2016 and judgment and order dated 24.01.2018 passed by the Administrative Tribunal. Inspite of the receipt of the aforesaid judgments and orders and repeated request of the writ-petitioner, the writ-respondents showed disobedience and disregard and commit-ted flagrant violation of the judgment passed by the High. Court Division and the writ-respondents willfully and deliberately did not comply with the direction of the judgment passed by the High Court Division. The writ-petitioner in these circumstances was constrained-to file Contempt Petition No.165 of 2018 before the High Court Division praying for drawing up contempt proceedings against the writ-respondents.
8. The High Court Division after hearing the parties verbally directed the writ-respondents through the learned Attorney General for Bangladesh to comply with the judgment and order dated 09.06.2016 and adjourned the matter as stand over. The writ-petitioner under such circumstances was apprehending a genuine threat of unnecessary harassment and embarrassment such as transfer, attachment, reduction in rank etc. and thereby filed an application before the High Court Division on 11.04.2018 praying for an order not to harass and/or embarrass the Writ-petitioner. While the above application was pending before the High Court Division the writ-petitioner was subjected to more inquiry by the Durnity Daman Commission which was commenced after the writ-petitioner filed the aforesaid contempt petition despite the facts that the Durnity Daman Commission conducted inquires seven times on different dates on the selfsame false, vague and fabricated complaint from a family rival and all of the above seven inquiries were concluded with the unanimous findings that the allegations are false, baseless and accordingly were kept with the record. The Ministry of Home Affairs subsequently also conducted inquiry into the allegations against the writ-petitioner and found allegations false and fabricated on 07.07.2014. The Durnity Daman Commission also reached an unanimous decision that the Writ-petitioner and his family had not owned and acquired an properties beyond the information disclosed in their income tax returns and thus they had not owned and acquired any property disproportionate to their known sources of income and it was confirmed by the memo dated 15.06.2015 signed by the Secretary of the Durnity Daman Commission.
9. The Inspector General of Police directed the DIG of Dhaka Range to inquire into the matter and submit a report and accordingly upon inquiry a report was submitted by the DIG on 06.07.2017 with specific findings that the allegations as referred to him are false and fabricated. The High Court Division upon hearing the above application verbally directed the writ-respondents through the learned Attorney General not to embarrass and harass the writ-petitioner, but the writ-respondents in sheer disregard to the above verbal order of the High Court Division issued impugned office order dated 09.05.2018 under the signature of the writ-respondent. No.5 transferring and attaching the writ-petitioner from his present post Commandant (Police Super) RRF, Dhaka to a non-existing post of Police Super at Police Directorate, Dhaka with malafide intention to deprive the writ-petitioner from discharging his present official responsibilities and functions and also to snatch away and curtail all the powers and duties he had been entrusted with the Commandant (Police Super) Range Reserve Force, Dhaka. Putting the writ-petitioner under attachment as Police Super at the Police Directorate, Dhaka did not have any power and duty. Moreover, there was no existence of such post having duties, powers, status and amenities which amounts to a reduction in rank. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances, finding no other alternative efficacious remedy, the writ-petitioner filed the writ petition before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule.
10. The writ-respondent No.4 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition saying that since the service record of the writ-petitioner is not clean and he was an accused in different Departmental proceedings and was punished by the authority the Departmental Promotion Committee, UPC did not consider his case for promotion to the post of Additional DIG in its meeting dated 27.12.2015 and thus his name did not find place in the promotion notice dated 23.12.2016.
11. Upon hearing both the parties and considering the connected papers on record, a Division Bench of the High Court Division disposed of the Rule by the impugned judgment and order dated 03.07.2018.
12. Feeling aggrieved, by the impugned judgment and order dated 03.07.2018 passed by the high Court Division in Writ Petition No.6326 of 2018, the Government and other-writ-respondents as appellants herein petitioners filed the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal. This Division after hearing the parties by judgment and order dated 19.01.2020 was pleased to grant leave and hence the instant Civil Appeal.
13. Mr. Sk. Mohammad Murshed, the learned Additional Attorney General appearing on behalf of the writ-respondents-appellants in Civil Appeal No.28 of 2020 took us through the judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 03.07.2018, the materials on record and submitted that the High Court Division erred in law by passing the impugned judgment and order inasmuch as it failed to appreciate that since the writ-petitioner as a public servant filed the writ-petition challenging his transfer which being terms and conditions of his service, is within the powers of the Administrative Tribunal and, therefore, the writ petitioner filed under Article 102(1) is barred under Clause (2) of Article 117 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Giving reference to the decision in the case of Government of Bangladesh and others Vs. Sontosh Kumar Saha and others, 21 131,C(AD)94, he next submitted that according to Article 117 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh the Administrative Tribunal has the exclusive jurisdiction to hear and determine the issues in respect of the terms and conditions of service of the Republic and without considering the same, the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and order dated 03.07.2018. The learned Additional Attorney General further submitted that the previous position of the writ-petitioner i.e. Commandant (Police Super), RRF, Dhaka and the transferred post of the writ-petitioner i.e. Police Super, Police Directorate, Dhaka carried equal status of Police. Super and, hence, no question of reduction of rank should arises and as such, the impugned judgment and order dated 03.07.2018 passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.
<u>14. Mr. Sk. Mohammad Murshed, the learned Additional Attorney General appearing on behalf of the petitioners in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1450 of 2021 also took us through the judgment and order of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal dated 11.03.2021, the materials on record and submitted that the Administrative Appellate Tribunal erred in law by passing the impugned judgment and order inasmuch as it misread and misconstrued the provision of law and materials on record causing miscarriage of justice. The learned Additional Attorney General lastly submitted that the Administrative Appellate Tribunal failed to consider that the respondent is a delinquent officer and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside.</u>
<u>15. On the other hand, Ms. Tania Amir, the learned senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the writ-petitioner-respondent in Civil Appeal No.28 of 2020 submitted that the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute and, thereby, directed the writ- respondents to consider the writ-petitioner's case to be promoted to the post of DIG in accordance with law with immediate effect and also declared the impugned notification bearing No.44.00.0000.09404.073.13 (Part-621) crated 09.05.2018 issued under the signature of the writ-respondent No.5 attaching the writ-petitioner to the non-existing post from the present post of Commandant (Police Super), Range Reserve Force, Dhaka to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and thereby set aside the same. She further contended that the writ-petitioner-respondent is a valiant and dedicated police officer, who stood 1st in Police Cadre in the 17th BCS Examination and subsequently joined the police service as an. apprentice Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) on 22.02.1998. Thereafter, the writ-petitioner successfully completed the departmental examination and the basic training in Sarda Police Academy and was awarded the Best Rider Prize. Later on, the appointment of the writ-petitioner was made permanent on 27.08.2000. He passed the Senior Scale Examination for promotion to the next higher post. He also completed some other courses and training in home and abroad and he was evaluated at more than 95% from the year 2010-2014 in the ACR. Apart from this, at the behest of some vested quarter the Anti Corruption Commission (ACC) investigated into the fake allegations against the writ-petitioner-respondent several times and submitted a report finding the writ-petitioner innocent.</u>
16. The learned Advocate next submitted that despite possessing all the requisite qualifications and extraordinary performance the writ-petitioner's name was left out from promotion list in the post of Additional Deputy inspector General of Police. Then and there the writ-petitioner-respondent took shelter of the High Court Division wherein it was directed the writ-respondents to include the name of the writ-petitioner in the list of promotion to the post of Additional DIG. Thereafter, upon preferring appeal before this Division at the instance of the writ-respondents it was disposed of with the observation to the effect that if the writ-petitioner wanted to redress his grievance before the Administrative Tribunal it should hear and dispose of the petition within 6(six) months from the date of filing of the case. Later on, the writ-petitioner filed a case before the Administrative Tribunal, which was allowed upon hearing on 24.01.2018 with a direction with retrospective effect to the writ-respondents to give the writ-petitioner promotion in the post of Additional DIG along with salary, other allowances, seniority and all other benefits.
17. The learned Advocate next submitted that although the Ministry of Law opined not to prefer appeal against the judgment of the Administrative Tribunal the writ-respondents filed appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, which was dismissed on 11.03.2021. The learned Advocate next contended that despite the respondent was innocent the appellants resorted to no-compliance of the judgment in favour of the respondent malafide with a view to harassing and depriving him from enjoying his legal right. The learned Advocate lastly submitted that the appellants disregarding the judgment of the Administrative Tribunal issued office order dated 09.05.2018 transferring and attaching him from his present post Commandant (Police Super), RRF, Dhaka to 4 non-existing post of Police Super, Police Directorate, Dhaka only to harass and undermine the image of the respondent violating the fundamental rights of the respondent, hence the High Court Division lawfully passed the judgment and order dated 03.07.2018.
<u>18. Mr. Probir Neogi, the learned senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in Civil Petition No.1450 of 2021 vehemently opposing the leave petition contended that the Administrative Appellate Tribunal rightly dismissed the appeal inasmuch as the Administrative Tribunal allowed the case after assessment of the evidences and materials on record. The learned Advocate lastly drew the attention of this Division that the petitioners had been resorting to multifarious tactics to harass and doing mischief to the respondent and this leave petition against the judgment and order of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal brought as a part of malicious plan of the petitioners.</u>
<u>19. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the sides in both the cases, perused the judgment and order dated 03.07.2018 passed by the High Court and also the judgment and order dated 11.03.2021 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal as well as the materials on record.</u>
20. It would be benefitted for all of us, if we go through the powers and jurisdiction of Administrative Tribunal as has been mentioned in section 4 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 which provides as follows:
"4. Jurisdiction of Administrative Tribunals-
(1) An Administrative Tribunal shall have exclusive jurisdiction to hear and determine applications made by any person in the service of the Republic (or of any statutory public authority in respect of the terms and conditions of his service including pension rights, or in respect of any action taken in relation to him as a pet-Son in the service of the Republic or of any statutory public authority).
(2) A person in the service of the Republic (or of any statutory public authority) may make an application to an Administrative Tribunal under sub-section (1), if he is aggrieved by any order or decision in respect of the terms and conditions of his service including pension rights or by any action taken in relation to him as a person in the service of the Republic (or of any statutory public authority).
Provided that no application in respect of an order, decision or action which can be set aside; varied or modified by a higher administrative authority under any law for the time being in force relating to the terms and conditions of the service of the Republic (or of any statutory public authority) or the discipline of that service can be made to the Administrative Tribunal until such higher authority has taken a decision on the matter.
Provided further that, where no decision. on an appeal or application for review in respect of an order, decision or action referred to in the preceding proviso has been taken by the higher administrative authority within a period of two months from the date on which the appeal or application was preferred or made, it shall, on the expiry of such period, be deemed, for the purpose of making an application to the Administrative Tribunals under this section, that such higher authority has disallowed the appeal or the application).
Provided further that no such application shall he entertained by the Administrative Tribunal unless it is made within six months from the date of making or taking of the order, decision or action concerned or making of the decision on the matter by the higher administrative authority, as the case may be.
(3)In this section "person in the" service of the Republic (or of any statutory public authority)" includes a person who is or has retired or is dismissed, removed or discharged from such service but does not incluide a person in the defence services of Bangladesh (or of the Bangladesh Rifles)."
21. Again, it is enshrined in Article 1.17 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in the following:
"Administrative tribunals-
117(1) Notwithstanding anything hereinbefore contained, Parliament may by law establish one or more administrative tribunals to exercise jurisdiction in respect of matter relating to or arising out of-
(a) the terms and conditions of per-sons in the service of the Republic, including the matters provided for in Part IX and the award of penalties or punishments;
(b)the acquisition, administration, management and disposal of any property vested in or managed by the Government by or under any law, including the operation and management of, and service in any nationalised enterprise or statutory public authority;  (c) any law to which clause (3) of article 102 applies.
(2) Where any administrative tribunal is established under this article, no court shall entertain any proceedings or make any order in respect of any matter falling within the jurisdiction of such tribunal: Provided that parliament may, by law, provide for appeals from, the review of decisions of any such tribunal.
22. From the above provisions of law it is abundantly. clear that Administrative Tribunal has the exclusive jurisdiction to deal with the matters when a person in the service of the Republic is aggrieved by any order or decision in respect of the terms and conditions of his service including pension rights or by any action taken in relation to him as a person in the service of the Republic. In the present case, the writ-petitioner-respondent is a person in the service of the Republic as per the provision of section 4(3) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 and he filed the writ petition challenging his transfer which relates to the terms and conditions of his service and as such the Tribunal had the exclusive jurisdiction to deal with the matter regarding the terms and conditions of service i.e., the promotion, transfer, posting etc. of the writ-petitioner-respondent. Again, according to Article 117(2) of the Constitution the writ-petitioner-respondent cannot invoke jurisdiction of any other court except the administrative tribunal in respect of the terms and conditions of his service.
23. Apart from this it is also unanimously settled by this Division that in the case of Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and other Vs. Sontosh Kumar Saha and others, 21 BLC(AD)(2016)94 that a public servant has no right to invoke the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh regarding the terms and conditions of his service and his grievances are amenable before the Administrative Tribunal constituted under Article 117(2) of the Constitution, even in case of malefide.
<u>24. It was further observed that in the aforesaid case that "We want to make in this connection that except on the limited scope challenging the uires of law or if there is violation of fundamental rights, the power of the High Court Division is totally ousted under Clause (5) of Article 102 read with Article 11.7(2). If a public servant or an employee of statutory corporation wants to invoke his fundamental rights in connection with his terms and conditions of service, he must lay foundation in the petition of the violation of the fundamental rights by sufficient pleadings in support of the claim. It will not suffice if he makes evasive statement of violation of his fundamental rights or that by making stray statements that the order is disputed question of fact and law, and the Tribunal is, therefore, competent enough to decide question of malafide or collusion or arbitrariness in taking the decision....Mere superficial pleadings on the point of fundamental rights will not confer any power on the High Court Division in respect of the terms and conditions of service."</u>
25. It transpires from the record that earlier the writ-petitioner respondent filed a case being A.T. Case No.243 of 2017 which was renumbered as A.T. Case No.170 of 2017 in the Administrative Tribunal due to the grievance as his name was left out from promotion list in the post of Additional Deputy Inspector General of Police. In due course, upon hearing the case the Administrative Tribunal allowed the case with a direction with retrospective effect to the writ-respondents to give the writ-petitioner promotion in the post of Additional DIG along with salary, other allowances, seniority and all other benefits. Later on, the writ-respondents-petitioners preferred appeal being A.A.T. Appeal No.92 of 20018, before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal against the said judgment and order of the Administrative Tribunal which was disallowed on contest. From the foregoing discussion it is crystal clear that the respondent has already successfully got efficacious remedy in the Administrative Tribunal relating to the terms and conditions of his service and thereby in the present case the respondent has ample opportunity to seek relief before the Administrative Tribunal. Moreover, the respondent failed to show vires of law or violation of his fundamental rights. Hence, we hold that the Writ Petition No.6326 of 2018 is not maintainable in the eye of law and, as such, the impugned judgment and order dated 03.07.2018 passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.
26. In view of the earlier discussions made in respect of Civil Appeal No.28 of 2020 and considering other materials on record, we are of the view that the High Court Division committed gross illegality in issuing Rule in Writ Petition No.6326 of 2018 and upon hearing making the Rule absolute directing the writ-respondents to consider the writ-petitioner's case for promotion to the post of DIG with immediate effect declaring the notification bearing No.44.00.0000.094.04.073.13(Part-621) dated 09.05.2018 was issued without lawful authority.
27. In the light of the observations made above, we find merit in the submissions of the learned Additional Attorney General appearing on behalf of the appellants in Civil Appeal No.28 of 2020 and, there-fore, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division on 03.07.2018 in Writ Petition No.6326 of 2018 is set aside.
28. Accordingly, the Civil Appeal No.28 of 2020 is allowed.
29. The Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1450 of 2021 is disposed of in the light of the observations made in Civil Appeal No.28 of 2020.
End.

Obaidul Hassan, J: All the Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal are disposed of by this common judgment as all of those involve common questions of law and similar facts.
Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2884 of 2022:
2. The Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2884 of 2022 has arisen out of interim order dated 17-10-2022 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.11693 of 2022 releasing the writ petitioners-respondents No.1-4 from Kashimpur Mahila Central Jail, Gazipur and Dhaka Central Jail till disposal of the Rule, who were confined in civil prison in connection with Artha Execution Case No.306 of 2021 arising out of judgment and decree dated 20-11-2018 passed in Artha Rin Suit No.915 of 2016, now pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 , Dhaka.
3. The necessary facts for disposal of the civil petition for leave to appeal, in a nutshell, are that the writ petitioners-respondents No.1-4 filed the said writ petition stating, inter alia, that the writ petitioners are law abiding citizen of Bangladesh and come of respectable families. On 8-12-2010 by a sanction letter bearing Reference No. প্রকা/এসএমইবি/শাখা/৬৯৭ the writ-respondent No. 3 sanctioned a package loan for the amount of Taka 15,26,50,000 (Fifteen Crore Twenty Six Lac and Fifty Thousand) and subsequently on 8-4-2012 by a sanction letter bearing Reference No. প্রকা/এসএমইবি/শাখা/২৪৪, the writ-respondent No.3 rescheduled loan to the amount of Taka 26,37,00,000 (Twenty Six Crore Thirty Seven Lac) in favour of the borrower where the writ-petitioners No.1-4 are the guarantors of the said facility. The writ-respondent No.3 approved the said loan in terms of the schedule property vide letter dated 27-12-2012. Due to unrest environment in the country, the business of the borrower faced huge loss and the borrower company became sick. In the meantime, the writ-respondent No.3 bank filed Artha Rin Suit No.01 of 2015 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka for recovery of outstanding dues against the borrower along with the guarantors. The defendants No.1-4 on 13-8-2015 filed written statement in the said case.
4. On conclusion of trial of the Artha Rin Suit, the Artha Rin Adalat on 18-11-2018 was pleased to pass ex-parte judgment in favour of the writ-respondent No.3 decreeing Taka 62,00,86,616.22 including interest @ 12% of the actual decreetal amount. It was also ordered that if the defendants fail to pay the decreetal amount within 60 days of the decree, the writ-respondent No.3 will be entitled to execute the said decree in accordance with law.
5. Thereafter, the writ-respondent No.3 filed Artha Rin Execution Case being No.133 of 2019 on 19-3-2019 before the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka praying for execution of the decree for realization of the decreetal amount. The writ-respondent No.3 subsequently filed another Artha Rin Execution Case being No.306 of 2021 before the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka praying for execution of the decree for realization of the decreetal amount (It is noted that the Artha Rin Execution Case No.133 of 2019 became merged with Artha Rin Execution Case No.306 of 2021). The writ-respondent No.3, Bank made an application before the Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka under section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 to issue warrant of arrest against the writ-petitioner and on 11-4-2022 the Court was pleased to allow the application.
6. The writ-petitioners No.2-4 were arrested and they filed an application for bail on 28-8-2022 before the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka and after hearing the same was rejected on 31-8-2022. Subsequently, the writ-petitioner No.1 was arrested and on 4-9-2022 filed an application for bail before the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka and after hearing, the same was rejected on the same date. The writ-petitioner is the wife of the defendant No.4 and writ-petitioners No.2-4 are 3rd party guarantor and have no interest in the loan and obtained no benefit from it. But yet, due to stipulation of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, they have been made defendants. The writ petitioners are willing to adjust the loan amount with installment. The writ-respondent No.3, Bank has applied for and obtained an order of civil confinement against the writ-petitioners.
7. In view of section 6(5) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 the third-party mortgagor's liberty should not be affected until all avenues against the borrower have been used, but now the writ-petitioners No.2-4 being a third-party mortgagor is in custody and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be declared illegal and without lawful authority so far as it relates to the writ-petitioners.
8. On 17-10-2022 a Division Bench of the High Court Division was pleased to issue Rule and interim order and it was further ordered that the writ-petitioners be released on bail from Kashimpur Mahila Central Jail, Gazipur and Dhaka Central Jail till disposal of the Rule.

Submission of the Counsels:
28. Mr Sk. Md Morshed, the learned senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner in all the Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal has taken us through the order dated 17-10-2022 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 11693-11696 of 2022, the materials on record. The learned senior Counsel submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in passing the impugned orders inasmuch as according to section 34 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the judgment-debtors are not entitled to be released on bail unless they have paid 25% of the decreetal amounts. The learned senior Counsel submits further that the impugned orders of the High Court Division shall open a flood-gate to release the judgment-debtors without payment of decreetal dues and the financial institutions will incur irreparable loss and, as such, those orders are liable to be set-aside.
29. Per contra, Mr M. Sayed Ahmed, senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents No.2-4 in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2884 of 2022, and the respondent No.1 in Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal No.2884-2887 of 2022 has seriously opposed the submissions advanced by the learned Counsels for the petitioners. The learned senior Counsel contends that the High Court Division on proper appreciation of law passed the impugned orders and, as such, the same cannot be interfered with by this Division. The learned senior Counsel finally earnestly craves for dismissal of the instant Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal.
Deliberation:
30. Suffice it to say that the aim of establishing Artha Rin Adalat is to streamline the loan recovery system and Artha Rin Adalat is regulated by Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. At this juncture, it is advantageous to discuss the provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereafter referred as Ain, 2003). Section 34 of Ain, 2003 is extracted below:
“৩৪ । দেওয়ানী আটকাদেশ ।-(১) উপ-ধারা (১২) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, অর্থ ঋণ আদালত, ডিক্রীদার কর্তৃক দাখিলকৃত দরখাস্তের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে, ডিক্রীর টাকা পরিশোধে বাধ্য করিবার প্রয়াস হিসাবে, দায়িককে ৬ (ছয়) মাস পর্যন্ত দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক রাখিতে পারিবে ।
(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর উল্লিখিত বিধান, মূল্য ঋণ গ্রহীতার মৃত্যুর কারণে পারিবারিক উত্তরাধিকার আইন অনুযায়ী স্থলাভিষিক্ত দায়িক-ওয়ারিশদের ক্ষেত্রে প্রযোজ্য হইবে না।
(৩) জারী মামলা কোন কোম্পানী (Company) যৌথ_কারবারী প্রতিষ্ঠান (Firm) অথবা অন্য কোন নিগমবদ্ধ সংস্থা (Corporate body) এর বিরুদ্ধে কার্যকর করিতে বিবাদী-দায়িককে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করা আবশ্যক হইলে, উল্লিখিত কোম্পানী, যৌথ কারবারী প্রতিষ্ঠান বা নিগমবদ্ধ সংস্থা আইন বা বিধি মোতাবেক যে সকল স্বাভাবিক ব্যক্তির (Natural) সমবয়ে গঠিত বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে, সেই সকল ব্যক্তি এককভাবে ও যৌথভাবে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটকের জন্য দায়ী হইবেন।
(8) উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান এইরূপ কোন ব্যক্তির বিরুদ্ধে কার্যকর হইবে না, যিনি ডিক্রীর সংশ্লিষ্ট ঋণ গ্রহণের পরবর্তীতে উত্তরাধিকার সূত্রে উপরি উল্লিখিত কোন ব্যক্তি বা ব্যক্তিবর্গের স্থলাভিষিক্ত হইয়াছেন।
(৫) উপ-ধারা (১) বা (৩) এর অধীনে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক কোন ব্যক্তি, ডিক্রীর দাবী সম্পূর্ণরূপে পরিশোধ না করা পর্যস্ত, অথবা ৬(ছয়) মাসের সময়সীমা অতিক্রম না হওয়া পর্যস্ত, যাহা পূর্বে হয়, দেওয়ানী কারাগার হইতে মুক্তি লাভ করিবে না, এবং ডিক্রীর সম্পূর্ণ টাকা পরিশোধ করার সংগে সংগে আদালত তাহাকে দেওয়ানী কারাগার হইতে মুক্তির নির্দেশ প্রদান করিবে ।
(৬) উপ-ধারা (৫) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক দায়িক যদি ডিক্রীদারের অপরিশোধিত পাওনার ২৫% এর সমপরিমাণ অর্থ নগদ পরিশোধ করিয়া এই মর্মে বন্ড প্রদান করেন যে, তিনি পরবর্তী ৯০ (নব্বই) দিবসের মধ্যে অবশিষ্ট পাওনা পরিশোধ করিবেন, তবে সেক্ষেত্রে আদালত দায়িককে মুক্তি প্রদান করিবে।
(৭) উপ-ধারা (৬) এ উল্লিখিত বন্ডের শর্ত মোতাবেক যদি দায়িক অবশিষ্ট পাওনা পরিশোধ করিতে ব্যর্থ হন, তবে তিনি পুনরায় গ্রেপ্তার ও দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক হইতে দায়ী থাকিবেন, এবং এইরূপ দেওয়ানী কারাগারে পুনরায় আটকাদেশ হইলে, উহা ছয় মাস পর্যস্ত বহালযোগ্য নতুন আটকাদেশ হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে ।
(৮) এই আইনের অধীনে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটককৃত ব্যক্তির ভরণপোষণ খরচ সরকার কর্তৃক বিচারাধীন আসামীর অনুরূপ খরচের ন্যায় বহন করা হইবে, এবং পরবর্তীকালে সরকার ডিক্রীদারের নিকট হইতে সরকারী পাওনা হিসেবে উক্ত খরচের অর্থ আদায় করিতে পারিবে, এবং ডিক্রীদার দায়িকের নিকট হইতে মামলার খরচ বাবদ উক্ত অর্থ আদায় করিতে পারিবে ।
(৯) এই ধারার অধীনে আদালত কোন দায়িককে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করার আদেশ প্রদান করিবে না, যদি না তৎপূর্বে অন্ততঃ একটি নিলাম বিক্রয় কার্যক্রম অনুষ্ঠিত হইয়া থাকে এবং উহার দ্বারা ডিক্রীদারের প্রাপ্য পরিপূর্ণভাবে আদায় হইয়া থাকে ।
(১০) যদি কোন কারণে উপ-ধারা (৯) এর অধীন একটিও নিলাম বিক্রয় কার্যক্রম অনুষ্ঠান করা সম্ভব না হয়, তবে সেই ক্ষেত্রে দায়িককে সরাসরি গ্রেফতার ও দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করা যাইবে ।
(১১) ১৮ (আঠার) বৎসরের কম বয়ষ্ক কোন ব্যক্তিকে এই ধারার অধীনে ডিক্রী কার্যক্রম করার নিমিত্ত গ্রেফতার এবং দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করা বা রাখা যাইবে না।
(১২) এই আইনের অধীনে কোন ডিক্রী বা আদেশ বাস্তবায়নের উদ্দেশ্যে পরিচালিত জারী মামলায়, জারী মামলার সংখ্যা একাধিক হইলেও, কোন একজন দায়িককে গ্রেফতার করিয়া পরিপূর্ণ মেয়াদের জন্য একবার দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক রাখা হইলে, তাহাকে পুনর্বার গ্রফতার করা ও দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করা যাইবে না।
(১৩) এই ধারার অধীনে কোন দায়িককে আংশিক বা পূর্ণ মেয়াদের জন্য দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক রাখার কারণে তিনি দেনার দায় হইতে মুক্ত গণ্য হইবেন না, এবং এই আইনের অধীন নির্ধারিত তামাদি দ্বারা বারিত না হইলে, তাহার বিরুদ্ধে নতুন করিয়া জারী মামলা দায়ের করা যাইবে ।”
<u>31. On plain reading of section 34(1) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereafter Ain, 2003) it is palpable that Artha Rin Adalat is empowered to confine the judgment debtor/s in civil prison for a period of 6(six) months to compel them to pay the decreetal amount. According to section 34(3) of Ain, 2003, if the borrower is a company, the natural person consisting of whom the said company is deemed to have been formed, shall, severally and jointly be liable to confinement in civil prison. Admittedly respondent No.1 in all Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal, is the shareholder, director, chairman, mortgagor and guarantor of the loan and respondents No.2, 3 and 4 in Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal No.2884 of 2022 are the mortgagors and guarantors of the loan and the concerned Artha Rin Adalat on conclusion of trial in respective Artha Rin Adalat Cases, decreed all the cases. Thereafter, Artha Rin Execution Cases were filed against the respondent No.1 in all Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal and respondent Nos.2, 3 and 4 in Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal No.2884 of 2022 and after issuing warrant of arrest they have been arrested and was ordered to be confined in civil prison for a period of 6(six) months as per section 34(5) of Ain, 2003. Again, under section 34(5) of Ain, 2003 the writ-petitioners are not entitled to be released on bail unless they deposit 25% of the total decreetal amount and also execute a bond to the effect that they will pay the rest of the decreetal amount within next 90(ninety) days. But in the cases in hand, the High Court Division without complying with aforesaid provisions of law, most illegally released the writ-petitioners on bail. In doing so, the High Court Division flouted the categorical provisions of law as stated in section 34 of Ain, 2003.</u>
32. In view of the discussion made above, we find merit in the submissions of the learned Counsel of the petitioners. Therefore, we hold that the impugned orders dated 17-10-2022 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 11693-11696 of 2022 warrant interference by this Division and, as such, the same have no countenance in the eye of law.
33. All the Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal are disposed of.
34. All the Rules issued by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 11693-11696 of 2022 are discharged.
The respondents No.2-4 in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2884 of 2022, and the respondent No.1 in Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 2884-2887 of 2022 are directed to surrender before the concerned Artha Rin Adalat at once.
End.
